10.1a — 2-Button Jam: Kickoff & Pitch

Jam season. First up: a constraint jam — your ENTIRE game reads exactly two inputs. Not two keys, TWO INPUTS, whatever they mean. Constraints breed creativity because they steal your excuses: with everything allowed, you start with nothing; with almost nothing allowed, you start with a puzzle.

Kickoff ~15 min

What counts as an input? Anything that becomes a signal: two keys, two buttons, one key + one mouse click, a touch's left half vs right half, keyboard-only arrow keys COUNT AS FOUR (banned!). Past-hit examples: one-button runners (flap = jump), one-button bosses (hold longer = higher jump), two-button fighters (left dodge, right attack). Every input you OWN, you must OWN COMPLETELY: timing, meaning in context, held vs. tapped.

Scoping rules for the 6-day jam (build days are 10.1b–10.1e):

  • ONE verb is a mechanic; TWO verbs is a game; THREE is a scope lie. You have two buttons. Your game has two verbs. Done.
  • Reuse what you own: any starter code, your palette class (9.2a), your jump feel (6.3a), your cooldown pattern. A jam is not a clean-slate test — it is a fluency test.
  • The pitch sells the IDEA in one sentence: "It's ___ where the only two buttons are ___ and ___."

Socratic

The starter's PlayerController reads: WASD, E, Space, mouse click — about eight inputs. Name TWO you would keep for a two-button game and what each MEANS when it is your only verb. Why does fewer inputs make each input's FEEL more important (think: 6.3a's mercies, but for buttons)?

Pitch & Vote ~25 min

Write your pitch card (10 min):

  1. One sentence: the game ("a cave where you can only DUCK and DASH")
  2. Two verbs and their feel words (duck = commitment, dash = panic)
  3. One image sketch: the screen at the most interesting MOMENT
  4. Reused parts list (what you borrow vs. build — the jam-ethics version of 9.10a credits)

Pitch (30 seconds each) — then team up by vote. Every pitch gets three public votes. Top pitches recruit; you may join any team that will have you. Rules: teams of 1–3, every member writes code (no idea-guy-only roles), and every game ships SOMETHING playable by 10.1d — a finished small game beats an ambitious folder.

Tinker: Tonight's homework

  1. Create the jam repo/folder + a jam README (pitch card pasted in).
  2. Write the INPUT table: button, context, meaning, feel — your whole spec is this table.

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Pitch a two-verb game in one sentence with feel words
  • Justify scope: two inputs, one core loop, shipped by 10.1d
  • List reused code honestly and your new code honestly
